oneliner.t: First-term Republican congressman from Chugiak, a software-company founder and investor, who has held Alaska's at-large seat since January 2025; Trump-endorsed, he led the Aug. 18, 2026 top-four primary with 44.6% and faces independent Bill Hill, Democrat Eric Hafner and Libertarian Jim McDermott in the Nov. 3 ranked-choice general.

born.note: Birthplace in both; exact date from Wikipedia; age 48 in the 2026 pamphlet is consistent.

hometown.t: Anchorage, Alaska (born there; raised mainly in Florida)

upbringing.t: Born in Anchorage to Nicholas J. Begich Jr., an author and business owner, and Starr Lyn Weed. After his parents divorced he moved to Florida, where he was raised by his maternal grandparents and attended The Master's Academy. He earned a BBA from Baylor University and an MBA from Indiana University, worked for Ford Motor Company (2002–2004, per his own pamphlet), and has lived in Alaska since 2004 (Anchorage to 2011, Chugiak since). His grandfather, Rep. Nick Begich Sr., and uncles Mark Begich (former U.S. senator) and Tom Begich (former state Senate minority leader) were Democratic officeholders; those are their records, not his. He is a Republican.

career.org: FarShore Partners (software development; workforce mostly in India)

career.role: U.S. Representative, Alaska at-large (Natural Resources; Transportation & Infrastructure; Science, Space & Technology)

platform.t: Runs on opening Alaska's oil, gas and minerals; credits the 2025 reconciliation law with mandating lease sales in the ANWR coastal plain, NPR-A and Cook Inlet; lists advancing the Alaska gasline and removing regulatory obstacles as next priorities.
Claims tax relief for tips, overtime, seniors and small businesses from his first term; frames his agenda around lowering costs and creating high-paying jobs.
Called the 2026 U.S.–Israeli war on Iran 'a necessary and targeted response' and said he supports regime change in Iran (Feb. 28, 2026 statement).
Co-sponsored the SAVE America Act (proof of citizenship to register; photo ID to vote), which passed the House Feb. 11, 2026.
In 2022 said he agreed with the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision and that the issue belongs to the states.
Opposes gun-control legislation; strong Second Amendment supporter (2022).
Introduced the American Reserve Modernization Act (May 2026) to create a strategic bitcoin reserve in the Treasury.
Did not answer any policy questions in the Alaska Beacon's 2026 candidate survey.

promises.t: End regulatory obstacles to development and create high-paying jobs.

record.t: Born Oct. 21, 1977 in Anchorage; raised mainly in Florida after his parents divorced.

claims.claim: BBA, Baylor University; MBA, Indiana University.

record.t: Wikipedia lists the same two degrees (no years given).

claims.claim: Founder and former executive chairman of FarShore Partners (2006–2024).

record.t: Wikipedia says he founded FarShore after graduate school and was executive chairman as of 2021. His House new-filer report (filed Aug. 2025) lists him as executive chairman with a 69% stake.

claims.claim: Founder and former managing partner of Dashfire.

record.t: Wikipedia says he co-managed Dashfire with two partners; his disclosure lists a 42% stake in Dashfire Management and a managing-member position.

claims.claim: Vice chair of the Natural Resources energy and mineral resources subcommittee.

record.t: Wikipedia lists him as vice chairman of the Energy and Mineral Resources subcommittee.

claims.claim: Vice chair of the Transportation and Infrastructure railroads, pipelines and hazardous materials subcommittee.

record.t: Wikipedia confirms T&I membership (aviation, railroads and maritime subcommittees) but not the vice-chair title.

claims.claim: Executive vice chair of the Congressional Western Caucus.
Board president of the Alaska Policy Forum, 2018–2021.

record.t: Wikipedia confirms he served on the board but does not give the title.

claims.claim: The 'Working Families Tax Cuts Act' reopened energy development in NPR-A, the Coastal Plain and Cook Inlet.

record.t: Wikipedia credits him with securing mandated oil and gas lease sales in the ANWR coastal plain, NPR-A and Cook Inlet in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025). Whether the statement's 'Working Families Tax Cuts Act' label refers to that law was not confirmed in sources opened. Actual lease-sale results were not checked.

claims.claim: Raised Alaska's share of federal resource revenue from 50% to 70%.

record.t: Wikipedia says the law raises Alaska's share of revenue from those federal leases from 50% to 70%, but only starting in 2035. The pamphlet does not mention the delay.

claims.claim: Delivered tax relief covering tips, overtime, seniors and small businesses.

record.t: No source on the law's tax provisions or his role was opened in this pass.

claims.claim: Has not bought or sold individual publicly traded stocks while in Congress (spokesperson, Oct. 2026).

said.where: spokesperson Silver Prout, quoted by Anchorage Press

record.t: His filing-year-2025 annual report lists only a Sept. 2025 sale of a private stake (Raken Inc., via FarShore Ventures III), and a June 2026 PTR lists one private-fund purchase (Listen Ventures IV). No transactions in his publicly traded holdings (Tesla, Graphite One, UCore, Tectonic) appear. A second 2026 PTR (July 7) listed by LegiStorm was not opened.

said.t: Pledged to champion responsible resource development.

did.t: Credited with mandated lease sales in ANWR coastal plain, NPR-A and Cook Inlet in the 2025 reconciliation law.

said.t: Pledged to ensure access to quality healthcare.

did.t: Voted against a three-year extension of ACA premium subsidies (one of 196 Republicans). Whether that conflicts with the pledge depends on how 'access' is defined; the record shows the vote, not its effect.

said.t: Spokesperson: no individual public-stock trades while in Congress.

did.t: Disclosures opened show only private-fund/private-stake transactions.

promises_prev.promise: Champion policies that promote responsible resource development.

evidence.t: The July 2025 reconciliation law mandated oil and gas lease sales in the ANWR coastal plain, NPR-A and Cook Inlet; Wikipedia credits him with securing them.

complicating.t: Enacted as part of a party-line package with many authors; the 70% revenue share does not start until 2035; lease-sale outcomes were not checked.

promises_prev.promise: Cut red tape and support small businesses and good-paying jobs.

evidence.t: Stated in his 2024 pamphlet; no specific measurable action documented in sources opened.

complicating.t: Vague promise; no outcome data reviewed.

entries.t: Said Biden is president but described a 'crisis of confidence' in election systems needing more transparency; did not allege specific fraud.
Did not sign the September 2025 discharge petition; voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act on Nov. 18, 2025 after Trump reversed course (427–1).
Supported Trump's 2025 strikes on Iranian nuclear sites.
Backed the 2026 war and regime change; opposed House war-powers resolutions (roll calls handled separately).

corp.t: Non-party committees (PACs) gave $1,028,577 in 2025–26 (19% of receipts) and $1.38M over his three federal cycles; the business-vs-ideological split isn't available from FEC summaries. A pro-crypto super PAC, Defend American Jobs, spent nearly $500,000 supporting him in July 2026 (its corporate funders were not opened here). He holds $500K–$1M in bitcoin and introduced a strategic-bitcoin-reserve bill; no reporting documents a link between the spending and that bill.

trades.period: 2025 annual report and 2026 PTR #20020055 (a 2026-07-07 PTR not opened)
trades.overlap_note: No reported trade falls in an industry his committees oversee. He HOLDS (no trades reported) small positions in two Alaska mineral developers — UCore Rare Metals ($15K–$50K; Bokan Mountain) and Graphite One ($1K–$15K; Nome-area graphite) — and a 20.49% stake ($1M–$5M) in Wrangell-St. Elias at Elliott Creek Inc., a mineral estate. His Natural Resources Energy and Mineral Resources subcommittee (vice chair) has jurisdiction over mining policy. No link between these holdings and an official act is documented.

note.t: Filing-year-2025 annual report (signed Aug. 13, 2026, after an extension): largest holdings are Earthpulse Press Inc. (17%, $1M–$5M; distributions $100,001–$1M in 2025), FarShore Partners ($1M–$5M, plus a $250K–$500K loan to it), Listen Ventures III ($1M–$5M), OnyxMP Growth Co. ($1M–$5M), Wrangell-St. Elias at Elliott Creek ($1M–$5M), and bitcoin ($500K–$1M). Sold a minority stake in Raken Inc. (construction software) for $250K–$500K in Sept. 2025. Only liabilities are his spouse's student loans ($25K–$65K). Lists a position as Fellow of the Club for Growth Foundation; no gifts or sponsored travel. Net-worth range is assets minus liabilities, excluding 'undetermined' items and sub-holdings of Dashfire, Eagle Street, FarShore Ventures and Emerald Horseshoe to avoid double counting; the Anchorage Press put assets at 'at least $7.4 million.' Earthpulse Press is his father's publishing company, which sold books on conspiracy topics and electronic acupuncture devices; Alaska Public Media reported Begich III is a passive 17% shareholder, and in 2024 Peltola's campaign and the state Democratic Party attacked him over the devices. The business is his father's; his own documented tie is the shareholding and income.

committees: Natural Resources (vice chair, Energy and Mineral Resources subcommittee)

Co-sponsored the SAVE America Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote; it passed the House.

note.t: Born in Anchorage in 1977 but raised in Florida; lived in Alaska continuously since 2004 (Anchorage 2004–2011, Chugiak since 2011), per his pamphlet.

checks.legal: News searches (court cases, lawsuits, ethics complaints) found nothing against him; Wikipedia lists no legal matters. CourtListener and Justia not reachable from this environment. House Office of Congressional Conduct pages errored. No House Ethics finding found in sources reviewed.

Dan Sullivan, Speaker Johnson and other House GOP leaders; Club for Growth, Freedom Caucus Fund and NFIB are cited there but not opened.
